content.title: About
content.content: Frankfurter is a boiled beef sausage traditionally made without smoking. It has a mild flavor, a slightly spicy aroma, and a firm yet tender texture. The product is usually served cold, sliced for sandwiches or as a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the German city of Frankfurt‑am‑Main, where similar sausages were first produced.
Beef frankfurter is often considered a leaner alternative to traditional pork sausages.
Despite the lack of smoking, the characteristic taste is achieved with spices such as nutmeg and cardamom.
In some countries the frankfurter is served as a cold cut in festive dishes.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Beef frankfurter provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains vitamin B12 and niacin, supporting nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The product contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beef.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sausage products often contain a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Nitrites and other preservatives may be used to extend shelf life and should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage can lead to growth of pathogenic bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the frankfurter thinly and serve in sandwiches, salads, cold platters, or as part of a charcuterie board. It can also be used in hot dishes, but this description focuses on the unheated version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frankfurter refrigerated at 0 °C–4 °C in its original packaging or an airtight container. Once opened, it is best consumed within 7–10 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
